question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal.
question.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{0\cdot 1+2\cdot 1+0\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=(1)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}], \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{0\cdot 1+2\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{2}=(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x$ or any other non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}\,x}{‖x‖\,‖{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x‖} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 0+2\cdot 2+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(1)=0.
$$

**Note:** The vector $x$ can be written as $x={a}_{1}-{a}_{2}.$ So, $x$ lies in the subspace spanned by $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$ Therefore, the projection of $x$ onto $S$ is $x$ itself and the angle between $x$ and the subspace is equal to $0.$
